title: Decidability of the full alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment
formal: Is satisfiability decidable for the full equality-free alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment AUF1 defined below, with arbitrarily many variables and arbitrary existential/universal alternation inside each permitted quantifier block?
definitions:
Use finite relational vocabularies of arbitrary finite arities, with no equality, constants or function symbols. A V-atom is a relation applied to variables whose set of distinct variables is exactly the finite set V; repetitions are allowed. Define AUF1 inductively. Every atom using at most one variable belongs to it, and the class is closed under Boolean combinations. If V={v1,…,vk} is nonempty and psi is a Boolean combination of V-atoms and already constructed AUF1 formulas whose free variables lie in V, then both Q1 v1 … Qk vk psi and Q2 v2 … Qk vk psi belong to AUF1, for arbitrary choices of each Qi from existential and universal quantification. In the second expression v1 is left unquantified; an empty block has its usual meaning. Bound variables can be renamed to avoid capture.

Thus all genuinely multi-variable atoms introduced in one block have the same variable set, and the block leaves at most one of its variables free. Boolean combinations of earlier formulas are allowed by the inductive grammar, not by an unstated ban on mixing unary subformulas. An input is a finite closed formula in this grammar. Satisfiability means a nonempty finite or infinite structure satisfies it. Decidability asks for one total Turing algorithm, with no running-time bound.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked decision procedure for all sentences in this grammar, or prove undecidability. Results requiring three variables, purely universal blocks, or blocks whose innermost quantifier is existential do not settle the full question.
context: This fragment extends one-dimensional uniform syntax by allowing alternation within blocks. The distinction between its full grammar and two decidable restrictions is essential.
why: This asks whether a broad syntactic extension of a decidable logic retains an algorithmic satisfiability boundary.

import_provenance.original_title: Decidability of the full alternating uniform one-dimensional fragment
import_provenance.original_statement: Is satisfiability decidable for the equality-free fragment AUF1, allowing arbitrary alternation inside quantifier blocks while retaining uniformity and at most one free variable after each block? Fiuk and Kieroński settle important restricted blocks and the three-variable subfragment, but leave the full fragment open.
